answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The beacon multiplier is published, charged in tundra, and ferrous lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2927 identities would post 3666 proofs and burn roughly 4 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
